identity.title: Topological Blindspots: Understanding and Extending Topological Deep Learning Through the Lens of Expressivity

problem.claim: The paper studies how expressively topological deep-learning architectures can learn topological properties of data supported on higher-order objects.

gap.claim: The authors identify limited prior understanding of TDL expressivity from a topological perspective, including whether common HOMP architectures capture fundamental topological and metric invariants.

contributions.claim: Analyzes HOMP expressivity and reports inability to capture diameter, orientability, planarity, and homology, plus limitations in exploiting graph lifting and pooling.
Introduces multi-cellular networks (MCN) and scalable MCN (SMCN); MCN is described as fully expressive, while SMCN targets better scalability and mitigates many HOMP limitations.
Creates benchmarks for learning topological properties of complexes and evaluates SMCN on them and on real-world graph datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is, to their knowledge, the first study of TDL expressivity from a topological perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HOMP cannot capture the listed diameter, orientability, planarity, and homology invariants.
The authors report that SMCN improves over HOMP baselines and expressive graph methods on the proposed benchmarks and real-world graph datasets.
The authors report that MCN can reach full expressivity, while scaling it to large data objects can be computationally expansive.

narrative_sequence.summary: TDL architectures are unified as higher-order message-passing methods for topologically structured data.
The paper examines HOMP and reports blindspots involving key topological and metric invariants, as well as graph lifting and pooling.
It introduces MCN and the more scalable SMCN, trading MCN's stated full expressivity against its computational cost.
It proposes topology-focused benchmarks and evaluates SMCN against HOMP and expressive graph methods on synthetic-style benchmarks and real-world graph datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects an expressivity diagnosis to specific invariants, then introduces architectures designed to address the identified limitations and evaluates them on matching benchmarks.

lessons.interpretation: A paper's argument is easier to assess when the limitation, proposed remedy, and evaluation target are explicitly aligned.
lessons.application: Map each claimed model limitation to a named property-level benchmark and state which baseline comparison tests the proposed remedy.
lessons.exception: This mapping is less suitable when the work is primarily conceptual or when no operational benchmark can represent the target property.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal expressivity definitions, proof conditions, benchmark construction, dataset details, or numerical improvement margins.
The scope of MCN's stated full expressivity and the exact computational scaling behavior are not given.
The abstract does not establish independent validity of the reported comparisons or the stated priority claim.
